chief_complaint: high fever, muscle aches, and a rash after a hiking trip
hpi_details: 28F presents with 4 days of high fever, severe myalgias, and a headache. Yesterday, she developed a pink macular rash starting on her wrists and ankles, which has now spread to her trunk. She returned from a camping trip in North Carolina a week ago.
ideas: thinks she got a bad bug bite

core_concepts: Tick-borne illness caused by Rickettsia rickettsii.
Classic rash starts on extremities (wrists/ankles) and spreads centrally, often involving palms and soles.
common_misconceptions: Waiting for a positive serology before treating (treatment must be empiric and immediate as it can be fatal).
dangerous_errors: Delaying Doxycycline therapy. Doxycycline is the drug of choice for all ages (even children) for RMSF.
management_principles: Start Doxycycline IMMEDIATELY if clinically suspected.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) Clinical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 28F with fever, headache, myalgias, and a centripetally spreading rash after camping in NC.
reference_soap.objective: T 39.2C. Blanching erythematous macules on wrists, ankles, palms, soles, and trunk.
reference_soap.plan: Start oral Doxycycline STAT. Draw Rickettsia serologies but do not delay treatment. CBC, CMP.

learning_objectives: Recognize the clinical presentation and immediate Doxycycline requirement for RMSF.

teaching.one_liner: Fever, headache, and a rash starting on wrists/ankles following tick exposure, requiring immediate empiric Doxycycline.

must_ask.say: Have you been hiking, camping, or spent time outdoors recently, and did you notice any tick bites?
Where did the rash start, and how has it spread?
How high has your fever been, and have you had muscle aches?
Have you had a headache along with the fever?
Have you felt confused, or noticed decreased urination?

history.answer: I have had a burning high fever and my whole body aches all over.
The fever started four days ago and has not let up since.
My temperature reached 39.2 degrees at home, and I have had severe shaking chills and heavy sweating.
I took acetaminophen and ibuprofen yesterday, but they barely brought the fever down at all.
My muscles ache terribly all over, especially in my thighs and calves, making it painful even to walk.
I have had a severe throbbing headache across my forehead and behind my eyes for the past four days.
Small pink spots appeared on my wrists and ankles yesterday, and now they have spread inward across my palms, soles, and torso.
I spent several days hiking through tall brush in North Carolina, though I do not recall seeing an attached tick or any black scab.
I feel completely oriented without any confusion, and my urine output has been normal without any darkening or swelling.
No, I have not had any cough, runny nose, sore throat, or shortness of breath.
No burning when I urinate, no frequent urination, and no flank pain.
I felt mild nausea with the high fever, but I have not had any vomiting, abdominal pain, or diarrhea.
I sweat heavily when my fever spikes, but I have not experienced unexplained weight loss.
No, I have not noticed any swollen lumps in my neck, armpits, or groin.
I returned from a five-day camping and hiking trip in North Carolina one week ago, but I have not traveled internationally.
None of the friends who camped with me are sick, and no one around me at work has a fever.
No, I have never had cancer, chemotherapy, or taken any steroid or immunosuppressive drugs.
I have no history of heart murmur or valve problems, and I have not had any dental work done recently.
No, I have not started any new prescription medications or over-the-counter pills recently.
I am in a monogamous relationship with my partner with no new sexual contacts, and I have never used illicit or intravenous drugs.
I do not have any chronic medical illnesses like diabetes, hypertension, or asthma.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I do not take any daily prescription medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or environmental triggers.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco or vaping products.
I drink one or two glasses of wine socially on weekends, but nothing heavy.
I work as an office graphic designer and live in an apartment with my partner.
Both of my parents are healthy, and there is no family history of autoimmune or chronic diseases.
My last menstrual period began two weeks ago, and my cycles are always regular every 28 days.
I have a copper intrauterine device in place for birth control, so there is no chance of pregnancy.
I think I might have been bitten by a bug or tick while camping in the woods.
I am worried this might be Lyme disease or another dangerous infection that could get worse.
I would like to get a blood test to identify what infection this is and start the right treatment today.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 115/75 mmHg, pulse 104 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, temperature 39.2 C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Posterior oropharynx is clear without erythema, exudate, or petechiae.
Both tympanic membranes are clear, intact, and translucent without erythema or effusion.
No cervical, submandibular, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy noted.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally without wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi.
Regular tachycardic rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.
Soft and flat abdomen with no tenderness, rigidity, or guarding in any quadrant.
No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly appreciated on deep palpation.
Blanching erythematous macules distributed over wrists, ankles, palms, soles, and trunk without central eschar.
Neck is supple without nuchal rigidity; Kernig and Brudzinski signs are both negative.
